title: AEO for B2B: How to Get on the AI Shortlist Before Sales Ever Hears From You
metaTitle: AEO for B2B: Get on the AI Vendor Shortlist
metaDescription: B2B buyers shortlist vendors in AI assistants before sales hears from them. Learn what AI cites, which questions each buyer role asks, and how to measure it.
shortAnswer: B2B companies get on the AI shortlist by answering every question a buying committee asks, not just "best vendor": security, pricing, fit and comparisons, each on a crawlable page and each backed by third-party sources that say the same thing. Surveys from 6sense and Forrester suggest the list is usually set before sales is contacted. Measure it by asking those questions, role by role, and counting how often you are named.
intro:
A buyer with a six-figure budget asks ChatGPT for the best vendors in your category for a 200-person fintech. Five names come back with one-line reasons. If you are not one of them, you do not lose in the demo; you lose before anyone tells you there was a deal.

This page is for B2B companies of any kind, including services firms and software vendors selling to committees. It covers what the data says about shortlists, why long buying cycles change AEO, what AI cites, a playbook and how to measure it. If you sell self-serve software, [AI visibility for SaaS](/for/saas) goes deeper on the shortlist mechanics and our crawler data.

sections.heading: How has the B2B shortlist moved into AI?
sections.body:
It has moved to the start of the journey. In 6sense's 2025 buyer survey, [the winning vendor was already on the buyer's Day One shortlist 95% of the time](https://6sense.com/science-of-b2b/buyer-experience-report-2025/), from nearly 4,000 responses across three regions. Forrester's 2026 report says [genAI searches are now the starting point for B2B buyers](https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/).

G2's survey of 1,076 software decision-makers puts numbers on the AI step: [51% start research with an AI chatbot more often than Google, and 69% chose a different vendor than planned](https://learn.g2.com/g2-2026-ai-search-insight-report) after a chatbot's guidance. All three firms sell to B2B vendors and rely on self-reported answers, and G2 covers software only. Treat the figures as direction.

What this means for you is simple. Sales is no longer where the list gets made; it is where the list gets confirmed.

![Group of adults having a business meeting around a wooden table with laptops and devices.](https://images.pexels.com/photos/3182784/pexels-photo-3182784.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Why is AEO different for long, multi-stakeholder buying cycles?
sections.body:
Because the committee asks AI a sequence of different questions, and you must win more than the first one. Forrester says the typical decision involves [13 internal stakeholders and nine external influencers](https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/), procurement is a decision-maker in 53% of cycles, and buyers check AI output with peers and experts.

Each role asks something different. These prompts are our illustrations, not survey data:

| Role | A prompt they might type | The page that must answer it |
|---|---|---|
| Champion | "Best [category] tools for a 200-person fintech" | Segment landing page, comparison pages |
| Security or IT | "Is [vendor] SOC 2 compliant? Does it integrate with Okta?" | Public trust and integration docs |
| Finance or procurement | "What does [vendor] cost for 150 seats?" | Pricing or a plain pricing explainer |
| End user | "What do users complain about with [vendor]?" | Review profiles, honest fit page |

You can win the shortlist and lose the committee's group chat. Disagreement across sources is the risk: G2 found [buyers treat consistent answers across chatbots as a trust signal](https://learn.g2.com/g2-2026-ai-search-insight-report) and dig deeper when they see inconsistency. If your price or compliance status differs between your site, a directory and a review profile, the engine will repeat whichever it retrieves.

sections.heading: What does AI cite for B2B?
sections.body:
Mostly sources you do not control. An arXiv study across verticals found AI search engines show [a systematic bias toward earned media over brand-owned content](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08919). In G2's survey, review sites were the second most-cited influence on shortlists, after chatbots.

For a B2B category, that usually means four source types:

- **Review and directory profiles.** G2 reports [45% of buyers call a review citation the most confidence-inspiring signal](https://learn.g2.com/g2-2026-ai-search-insight-report) in an AI answer.
- **Roundups and analyst or trade coverage.** Forrester advises that providers should make claims that [trusted external voices can validate](https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/).
- **Community threads and partner pages.** Marketplaces, integration partners and indexed forums describe you in someone else's words.
- **Your own pages** with facts a model can lift: who you serve, pricing, security, integrations, results.

Mentions in these places count for more than links to your homepage, as we argue in our piece on [brand mentions](/blog/brand-mentions). The practical consequence: a firm with no review profile, no case-study numbers and no third-party coverage gives the engine nothing to cite, however good its website is.

Services firms feel this first. A prompt like "best [service] provider for a mid-size manufacturer" has no spec sheet to compare, so engines lean on what others say: case studies, directory listings, partner pages and press. A named result with a number and a timeframe is quotable. "We deliver excellence" is not.

sections.heading: What is the B2B AEO playbook?
sections.body:
Map the questions, publish ungated answers, prove claims with numbers, then earn outside coverage. In this order:

1. **Build the question tree from real sources.** Use discovery calls, RFPs and security questionnaires. Group questions by role and stage.
2. **State the entity plainly.** One paragraph on who you serve, what you do, what it costs and who you are not for. Google says [Organization markup helps disambiguate your organization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization); use it, but the plain text carries the weight.
3. **Ungate your best answers.** A PDF behind a form cannot be read by a crawler. Put the security summary, integration list and pricing logic on public pages.
4. **Prove it with real numbers.** Publish case studies with named metrics and customer permission. In the GEO paper, adding statistics and cited sources produced [30-40% visibility gains](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) on its benchmark.
5. **Write honest comparisons, one page per question.** One page per real rival, saying who should pick whom. A single "best tools" page cannot cover a question tree, and five thin pages on one question lose to one strong page: on 3 October 2026 we merged 165 of our own pages into 42, a lesson we stand behind.
6. **Earn the outside sources.** Update review profiles, brief analysts and pursue roundups the engines already retrieve.

Our view: skip the schema sprint and the gated whitepaper. The [AEO strategy guide](/blog/aeo-strategy) covers how to prioritize these decisions.

![Man drawing a pie chart on paper beside a cup of coffee, planning on a desk.](https://images.pexels.com/photos/7964208/pexels-photo-7964208.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do you measure B2B AEO?
sections.body:
Ask the committee's questions, role by role, many times, and report how often you are named. One answer is a sample: in SparkToro's 2,961 runs, [the odds of seeing the same brand list in two responses over 100 runs were under 1 in 100](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/) for ChatGPT and Google's AI. Its author still concluded that percent visibility across repeated runs is probably a reasonable measure.

Split the prompt set by stage. Discovery prompts ("best vendors for...") test whether you make the list. Validation prompts ("is [vendor] secure", "[vendor] vs [rival]") test whether you survive scrutiny. You can pass one and fail the other.

Log four things per prompt: named or not, framing, which competitors appear, and whether the facts are right. Wrong facts matter in B2B; G2 reports 64% of buyers see inaccuracies a few times a month or more.

Why first place matters: in AEOeye's audit records (a recommendation benchmark of 127 audits and 892 answers; self-selected, small, engines not comparable), answers named 2.9 competitors on average and 71.4% of 147 ranked mentions were first. Our [measurement guide](/blog/ai-brand-recommendation-measurement) shows how to code answers.

AEOeye's [free audit](/) asks three unbranded buyer questions to ChatGPT; the $29 report adds four engines and ten questions, one-time. It does not run role-by-role prompt sets daily. For that, use a dedicated tracker.

keyTakeaways: Surveys from 6sense, Forrester and G2 suggest the shortlist is set before sales is contacted; all are self-reported.
Buying committees ask AI different questions by role, so one "best vendors" page cannot cover them.
AI leans on earned sources: review profiles, roundups, analyst and community coverage.
Ungated, consistent, number-backed pages give engines something accurate to cite.
Measure by role and repeat runs, and report named-rate with its denominator.

faqs.q: Is AEO worth it for a B2B company with low search volume?
faqs.a: Often yes. Few buyers search, but each represents a large deal, and shortlists are short, so a place on one matters. AI answers named about three competitors per answer in our benchmark, which is small and self-selected. Check your own prompts first: if you are already named, protect accuracy; if not, fix source coverage.

faqs.q: How is B2B AEO different from B2B SEO?
faqs.a: SEO earns a ranked link a buyer may click. AEO earns a mention inside an answer, and that answer leans on third-party sources such as reviews and roundups. The fundamentals overlap, since Google says SEO basics still apply to its AI features, but you also have to be consistent and present on sources you do not own.

faqs.q: How do I know whether ChatGPT or Perplexity already recommends my company?
faqs.a: Ask the questions your buyers ask: category, comparison, security and pricing, phrased for your segment, on every engine and more than once. Note whether you are named, how you are framed and which sources are cited. AEOeye's free audit runs three unbranded questions on ChatGPT and shows the answers in full.

faqs.q: Which content helps a B2B company most?
faqs.a: Pages that answer the committee's real questions without a form: pricing logic, security and integration details, honest comparisons, and case studies with named numbers. They give engines facts to quote, and they match the stages where buyers validate a shortlist. Pair them with up-to-date review profiles.

faqs.q: How long does B2B AEO take to work?
faqs.a: No one can promise a timeline. Changes show up only after new pages or third-party mentions are published, crawled and retrieved, which depends on each engine and source. Measure a fixed prompt set before and after, run it repeatedly, and judge progress on the rate you are named, not on a single answer.
